# TASK-616: Contain verification descendants and enforce resource budgets

## Metadata

- Kind: `risk-control`
- Level: `5`
- Wave: `1`
- Workstream: `safety`
- Selection: `primary`
- Execution: `implemented`

## Goal

Repair the verification boundary exposed by a timed-out Swift test leaving an orphaned XCTest using 86.9G footprint. Account for owned descendants even after group/session changes or early parent exit, enforce finite budgets, and prove cleanup before candidate, mutation or scale execution resumes.

## Deliverables

- One enforced supervision contract across test entry points
- Machine-readable cleanup/resource evidence and regression fixtures
- A documented safe bootstrap and rerun procedure

## Allowed Write Scope

- Scripts/Testing/**
- docs/reliability/handoffs/harness/**
- Tests/PerformanceTests/**
- docs/reliability/evidence/TASK-616/**

## Non-Goals

- No broad process termination, production app restart, user-file cleanup, installation or release.
- No rerun of an unbounded memory/hang mutation to prove the guard works.

- None

## Validation Commands

- Bootstrap only bounded synthetic supervision fixtures under an independent watchdog; do not start existing Swift/mutation/scale runners before containment is proven.
- After synthetic acceptance, execute a snapshot-isolated bounded Swift/XCTest smoke through the repaired supervisor, then the focused supervisor regression suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AC-TASK-616-01` — Establish evidence-backed ownership of every launched test descendant before relying on termination: cover Swift-to-XCTest launch behavior, parent exit, group/session escape, identity/PID reuse and unrelated-process sentinels. Stop admission and report failure when ownership or measurement cannot be established. Never use broad name/path pkill or signal unrelated apps/tests.
- `AC-TASK-616-02` — Enforce explicit finite per-stage wall time, aggregate owned-process memory, output and termination-grace limits. Memory accounting must not silently equate RSS with total macOS physical footprint or omit escaped children. Record the measured metric, limitations, thresholds, peak, stop reason and cleanup result; retain the existing bounded log and credential-free environment.
- `AC-TASK-616-03` — On timeout, memory/output breach, cancellation, supervisor-handled error or early launcher exit, stop owned descendants, escalate within the bounded grace period as needed, and independently verify their exit. A report cannot claim success or completed cleanup while any owned process remains; include remaining identities if cleanup fails.
- `AC-TASK-616-04` — First exercise supervisor logic with small synthetic fixtures and an independent safety watchdog: each pathological fixture has a <=30-second outer deadline, <=256 MiB allocation ceiling, finite process count and its own terminal deadline. Cover a detached child, retained stdout, TERM refusal, measurement failure, PID-identity mismatch and an unrelated-process sentinel. Do not recreate multi-GB pressure or the old unbounded Swift hang.
- `AC-TASK-616-05` — Route focused, mutation, full-candidate, packaged-candidate, rollback and soak/scale test entry points through the proven supervision contract or fail closed before launching an unsupported path. Inventory bypasses, choose and justify finite build/test defaults, then run a bounded real Swift/XCTest smoke case and verify no descendant remains. Refresh safety documentation; no product changes or live-store access.

## Required Evidence

- `EVREQ-TASK-616-01` (regression-evidence) — Identity-bound process lifecycle reports for every synthetic failure case and the bounded real Swift/XCTest smoke, including thresholds, exact commands, exit verification and untouched sentinels.
- `EVREQ-TASK-616-02` (regression-evidence) — Before/after regression evidence demonstrating the original cleanup gap without unbounded memory or hangs; snapshot hashes and an inventory of all covered entry points. Historical green suites are not containment proof.
